# Subscription Agreement: Tansley Parcel

## 1. Parties and Record Dates

This Subscription Agreement is entered into by Pemberline Systems and Tansley Parcel for the subscription to Pemberline Dock described below. Pemberline Dock is Pemberline Systems’ yard and dock scheduling software.

This Agreement was drafted on 2025-01-08. This executed record was written on 2025-01-20. Both parties signed this Agreement on 2025-01-20. The effective date is 2025-02-01; the execution date and effective date are distinct.

## 2. Subscription and Term

Tansley Parcel subscribes to 110 seats of Pemberline Dock. The subscription is priced per seat per year.

The current subscription term begins on 2025-02-01 and ends on 2026-01-31. The end of the current term, recorded as the renewal date, is 2026-01-31.

The subscribed quantity shall be recorded as 110 seats in the subscription record, billing worksheet, and access-allocation register. Operational lists identifying users by shift or location shall refer to that subscribed quantity rather than treat each shift roster as a separate subscription.

## 3. Price and Discount

The price per seat per year is USD 1,800. A discount of 10% applies to the subscription.

For 110 seats, the annual amount before discount is USD 198,000. The discount is USD 19,800, resulting in a discounted annual subscription amount of USD 178,200.

The billing worksheet shall display the seat quantity, annual unit price, discount percentage, and discounted annual amount as separate entries so that Tansley Parcel may reconcile the invoice against this Agreement.

## 4. Payment Terms

Payment terms are net 30 days. Invoice preparation shall use the subscription particulars set out in Sections 2 and 3.

Procurement correspondence concerning invoice routing shall identify Tansley Parcel by its full name. Lev Arkadin, Procurement lead, is the customer contact for the administrative exchange of billing instructions

# Central weekly 1/5/26

Happy new year, everyone! Hope you all had a restful break and survived the inbox avalanche this morning. Here is where the Central pod stands for the week of 5 Jan 2026.

| Account | Focus this week | Next milestone |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Marrow Fieldworks | Ownership transition to Tobias Rendle | Intro call with Salina yard leads on 7 Jan 2026 |
| Tansley Parcel | Renewal paperwork and procurement review | Renewal due by 31 Jan 2026 |
| Marrow Agrisupply | Pooled queue coverage | Ticket #4418 fix on 8 Jan 2026 |

**Account handoffs and renewals**

Today is the official transition day for Marrow Fieldworks. We finished moving the open tickets and CRM tasks over from Pree's old dealer account before lunch. Tobias's dealer account has a Thursday morning check-in scheduled so the Salina and Kearney equipment yards can meet him and review their winter Combine Bay B gate schedules. 

With that handoff wrapped up, Pree is focusing on the Tansley Parcel renewal, which is due by 31 Jan 2026. Lev Arkadin asked for a clean export of their Q4 gate-house check-in logs at the Little Rock hub before he sends the paperwork through his legal queue. The account Pree runs also has two night-shift dispatchers requesting updated PDF printouts for the South Dock Door 14 kiosk, so she is sending those training sheets over this afternoon.

**Pooled queue notes**

On Marrow Agrisupply, whoever pulls the afternoon rotation today should check Ticket #4418. Their Topeka feed warehouse reported that the Gate 3 barcode scanner is dropping carrier check-ins when drivers arrive more than twenty minutes early for fertilizer drops. Let's get a reproduction log over to support before the 6 Jan 2026 morning standup.

# RCA: carrier API outage (Sept 3)

**From:** Priyanka "Pree" Sundaram <psundaram@pemberline.com>
**To:** Lev Arkadin <larkadin@tansleyparcel.com>
**Cc:** Hollis Mbeki <hmbeki@pemberline.com>
**Date:** 4 Sep 2025, 09:42 CDT
**Subject:** Re: RCA: carrier API outage (Sept 3)

Hi Lev,

Hope you are surviving the Thursday morning rush! And more importantly, hope the Tulsa yard is back to breathing normally today after yesterday's chaos. I promised I would get you the root-cause write-up from our platform folks as soon as they finished their post-mortem coffee, so here is the full scoop on what happened on 3 Sep 2025.

Basically, at 06:14 CDT yesterday, a routine worker node patch in our US-Central cluster introduced a bad retry loop on the carrier webhook listener inside Pemberline Dock. Whenever an inbound manifest ping timed out—which happens plenty during the 6am shift change—instead of backing off, the service fired immediate duplicate retries. That flooded the queue and locked up the live gate check-in screen for Tansley Parcel until engineering rolled the patch back at 07:48 CDT (ticket #INC-8841). 

I know that ninety-four minutes right at morning dispatch meant your guards at Doors 12 through 18 had to go back to clipboards and radio checks while five linehaul rigs backed up onto the service road. Nobody wants to be out in that humidity squinting at paper BOLs. To make sure this doesn't bite us again, engineering has already capped retry concurrency and split the webhook queue off from the main dock board service.

Because we obviously dropped the ball during your peak window, Hollis and I spoke with June Osei-Lark on our side this morning, and we want to put a goodwill service credit on your next invoice. Just reply with a quick thumbs-up if you are good with us applying that credit, and I will have June get it squared away with Stoneharrow Billing today.
